question: The AAIB records show Matrice 30T drones hitting power lines after a lost link. What should pilots set up to prevent this?
stop_reason: claims still failing after the revision limit

intake.focus: lost-link prevention and fail-safe configuration (RTH, altitude, geofencing)
intake.reason: AAIB example involves loss of link and subsequent collision; provide guidance from M30T manuals and FAA guidance on configuring fail-safe/return-to-home to prevent power-line strikes.

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance indicates that after loss of VLOS, the remote PIC must determine an action and may need to land, hover, or initiate a return-to-home sequence, with emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link. The DJI Matrice 30T manual notes that action on signal loss can be set to RTH, land, or hover, with Failsafe RTH triggering after six seconds if Home Point and compass are functioning and recorded, and it emphasizes setting an appropriate failsafe altitude and operating within the transmission range. Incident reports (unverified) mention RTH at a programmed altitude without issue when the link is lost and another note of RTH initiated but not responding, followed by manual regain and landing.
